references.text: Both verses mark critical transitions in Jacob's life where he asks to leave Laban, first after the marriage promise and later after completing his period of service.
The verses form a coherent sequence of events where 29:15 establishes the wage agreement and 29:21 demands its fulfillment.
The verses describe respectively the demand for the fulfillment of the marriage and its actual execution.
Creates a narrative contrast where Jacob first claims his wives as his right (29:21), while Laban later accuses him of stealing them (31:26).
Highlights the transition from Jacob's own desire to return home to God's direct command for the same journey.
Creates a thematic contrast between Jacob's claim to free himself from Laban's ownership (29:21) and Laban's assertion of continued ownership (31:43).
